headline: NMC Reopens Window For Eligibility Certificate Applications, Apply From April 6
body: Candidates have been advised to complete the application process carefully, as "incomplete applications in any form will not be processed and shall be summarily rejected."
full_body:
The National Medical Commission (NMC) has announced a fresh opportunity for students seeking Eligibility Certificates from the Ethics and Medical Registration Board (EMRB), allowing those who missed the earlier deadline to apply again.

In an official public notice, the Commission said the decision was taken after receiving representations from candidates who were unable to submit their applications earlier due to "technical issues".

According to the revised schedule, the online application window will reopen on April 6 at 10am and remain active till April 13 up to 6pm. Applications can be submitted through the official NMC portal.

"Keeping in view the career prospects of the applicants, it has been decided... to give an additional opportunity to the candidates," the notice stated.

Candidates have been advised to complete the application process carefully, as "incomplete applications in any form will not be processed and shall be summarily rejected." 

The Commission also clarified that it will not be responsible for such rejections. Officials further urged applicants not to wait until the last date. 

"Candidates may not wait for the last date to apply and should submit their applications as early as possible," the notice said, highlighting that the issuance process involves multiple levels of verification to ensure compliance with existing regulations. Applicants are also required to regularly check their registered email IDs and the online portal for updates regarding their application status.

The EMRB had earlier closed the application window on March 31, 2026, following a prior notice issued on February 27.

headline: Pakistan To Repay $3.5 Billion To UAE This Month Amid Strained Ties: Report
body: New Delhi, April 4 (IANS) Pakistan’s already weak economy is coming under fresh pressure as the country prepares to repay $3.5 billion to the United Arab Emirates this month, even as relations between the two sides show signs of strain.
full_body:
Pakistan's already weak economy is coming under fresh pressure as the country prepares to repay $3.5 billion to the United Arab Emirates this month, even as relations between the two sides show signs of strain.

According to a report by The Express Tribune, Islamabad has decided to return the loans in phases throughout April.

The report said that around $450 million will be paid next week, followed by $2 billion and another $1 billion later in the month.

The move comes after months of uncertainty over these loans. Unlike in the past, when Gulf countries often gave Pakistan more time to repay, the UAE had only been extending the loans for short periods. This change signals a tougher stance from a long-time ally.

The repayment is expected to put pressure on Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves, which are already under stress.

Using reserves to pay back such a large amount could weaken the country's ability to manage its external finances.

The situation has become more serious due to recent tensions with United Arab Emirates. Reports suggested that Abu Dhabi is unhappy with Pakistan's perceived closeness to Iran during the ongoing regional conflict.

This has raised questions among Emirati officials about Pakistan's foreign policy priorities.

headline: Gujarat Man Kicked On Chest, Strangled To Death For Refusing To Lend Rs 10
body: According to the FIR, Dharmendra demanded Rs 10 for personal expenses, and when Rajeshbhai refused to give the money, the encounter turned deadly.
full_body:
In a chilling display of violence over a trivial amount, a 41-year-old man was allegedly murdered in Bhadarwa village of the Narmada district, Gujarat, on Friday morning.

The victim, Rajeshbhai Dhanjibhai Tadvi, who suffered from physical disabilities including partial paralysis, was returning home with groceries from the village bus stand when he was intercepted by 33-year-old Dharmendrabhai (alias Dhamo) Ganpatbhai Tadvi.

According to the First Information Report (FIR), Dharmendra demanded Rs 10 for personal expenses, and when Rajeshbhai refused to give the money, the encounter turned deadly.

Eyewitnesses reported that the accused, Dharmendra, pinned Rajeshbhai down on an RCC road near the village entrance. He then brutally attacked Rajeshbhai, kicking him in the chest and neck before placing his foot on Rajeshbhai's throat to strangle him. The victim died on the spot due to his injuries, which included visible bruising and marks on his shoulders and neck.

Following the incident, the village sarpanch (head) alerted the local police, who arrived to find the victim's body covered in a shroud. The police, led by Inspector AP Solanki, have registered a case of murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against Dharmendra Tadvi.

The complainant, Bharatbhai Tadvi, expressed shock, noting that his cousin was targeted despite his vulnerable physical condition.

headline: Telegram’s Durov says Russia triggered payment system problem by blocking VPNs
body: Telegram said Moscow is trying to force Russians to use MAX, a state-backed messenger app schools and universities have been told to use
full_body:
Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

Telegram’s billionaire founder, Pavel Durov, said on Saturday that ⁠Russia’s attempt to block Virtual Private Networks (VPN) triggered a problem with a domestic payment system, adding that tens of millions of Russians were resisting digital controls.

Russia has repeatedly blocked mobile internet and granted sweeping powers to cut off mass communications while jamming messenger services and VPNs in ⁠what diplomats have called a “great crackdown”.

Friday’s technical problem, ⁠which Russia has yet to fully explain, sowed chaos for some shoppers, forcing the Moscow metro to allow entry without payment through its turnstiles, while a regional zoo had to ask visitors to use cash.

“Welcome back to the Digital Resistance, my Russian brothers and sisters,” Durov said on Telegram. “The entire nation is now mobilised to bypass these absurd restrictions.”

Russia’s biggest bank, Sberbank, said there was a technical issue on Friday but gave no details. Some Russian media ⁠deleted reports that the outage stemmed from state bids to block certain sites or VPNs.

Russian officials say the clampdown on VPNs and messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Telegram is essential for security as Moscow faces deadly attacks deep inside Russia from Ukraine and alleged attempts at sabotage by Western intelligence agencies.

Russia has slowed down Telegram, which has more than 1 billion active users and is also widely used in Ukraine, and investigated Durov in a criminal case involving accusations of terrorism.

headline: Delhi govt tightens noose for fuel supply: Businesses to get LPG only if they apply for PNG connection
body: Delhi's commercial LPG supply now requires users to register for piped natural gas (PNG) where available, or declare intent to switch. Oil marketing companies will verify these applications, sharing data with IGL. Businesses needing both can seek exemptions, ensuring compliance with the government's push for PNG adoption.

headline: Chinese CCTV camera ban shakes Hyderabad trade; Indian brand prices surge, stock piles up, sales drop
body: Demand shifts to Indian CCTV brands, discussions on replacing Chinese systems begin across government and large projects
full_body:
Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

The Centre’s ban on the import and sale of internet-connected CCTV cameras from Chinese manufacturers has begun to reshape Hyderabad’ s surveillance equipment market, with traders and installers reporting immediate disruptions in pricing, supply and customer behaviour.

At Gujarati Galli in Koti and Chenoy Trade Centre (CTC) in Secunderabad, key wholesale hubs largely driven by Chinese CCTV camera sales, the impact is already visible in lower volumes, unsold stock and rising price of alternatives. The ban came into force on April 1.

headline: 'Factually incorrect': India rejects 'payment issues' claim over Iranian crude tanker's diversion to China
body: Reports of an Iranian crude oil shipment rerouted to China due to payment issues have been officially denied by India's Petroleum Ministry. The ministry clarified that such diversions are common in global oil trade for optimization and assured that Indian refiners have secured their energy supplies, including from Iran, with no payment hurdles.
